clue.text: Jack Brown's design

blocks.note: a jack and a tar are both old words for a sailor
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack Brown has come up with a design.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Brown reads as a person's name, but each word is a separate piece; the 's joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is a pattern of crossing coloured stripes, the chequered design of Scottish plaid cloth.

clue.text: Compliment family taking the brothers back in

indicators.note: back says read the abbreviation for the brothers from right to left
taking means accepting inside, so the family word holds the other piece

blocks.note: a tribe is a family group or clan
trade unionists call each other brother, so the brothers are the TU, trade union

explanation.surface: A family pays someone a compliment by taking the brothers back in.
explanation.walkthrough: Union members traditionally address each other as brother, so the brothers stands for the trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribute is an expression of praise or admiration, essentially a compliment.

clue.text: Send the man with the stopwatch up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a timer is a person who times events with a stopwatch

explanation.surface: An instruction to send the official with the stopwatch upstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit is to send, especially money or a matter to an authority for decision.

clue.text: Pardon little woman sent running inside

indicators.note: running suggests letters on the move into a new order
inside places the jumbled word within the name

blocks.note: Amy March is the youngest of the four sisters in Little Women
taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea to forgive a small woman who has been sent away running.
explanation.walkthrough: Little woman points to Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women, whose youngest sister is Amy.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is an official pardon granted to a group of offenders.

clue.text: Initially Purgatorio by Dante edited by fussy academic

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows it
an edited text has been reworked, so the poet's name is rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of Purgatorio
the poet's name taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A fussy scholar has edited Purgatorio, the second part of Dante's Divine Comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone overly concerned with minor details and rules, typically of learning.

clue.text: When ten television moguls come to an understanding?

indicators.note: moguls own and hold things, so the clue's words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: Asks when ten TV bosses will ever reach an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding or informal agreement, especially between nations.

clue.text: Clumsily, a Welsh king battles with daughter, heartless lady

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letters are taken out of the following word

blocks.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for Welsh
K is the chess abbreviation for king
to war is to fight, so battles is read as the verb
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written, then its middle removed

explanation.surface: A Welsh king clumsily fights alongside his daughter, a cold-hearted woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Battles is a verb here (he battles), and its root verb war supplies the piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkwardly is the adverb for doing something in an ungainly or clumsy manner.

clue.text: One who promises to give you a bell, a little one?

definitions.text: One who promises to give you a bell, a little one?

blocks.clueFragment: One who promises to give you a bell
blocks.note: surface reading: someone who says they'll phone you, a bell being British slang for a phone call
setter's reading: a small phone call is a tinkle, so the person promising one is named after that

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang both a bell and a tinkle mean a phone call; a tinkle is the lighter, smaller ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rings with a light tinkling sound, here the person giving you a quick call.

clue.text: He proclaimed woman and lad misbehaving

indicators.note: misbehaving means acting out of order, so these letters fall out of order

blocks.note: her is a pronoun standing for a woman
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A man announces that a woman and a boy have been naughty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the person who did the proclaiming: he who proclaimed.
explanation.definitionFit: A herald was an official messenger who made public announcements.

clue.text: Resolute pledge by funeral directors' business?

blocks.note: first meaning: a promise one is determined to keep
second meaning, whimsically: a company that arranges burials

explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as noun plus noun: a firm is a business and undertaking is the trade of funeral directors; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm undertaking is a solid promise, and also, punningly, an undertaker's company.

clue.text: Military governors? Just an aberration

indicators.note: an aberration is a departure from the normal, so the letters stray from their usual order

blocks.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: Rule by generals is dismissed as merely an aberration.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a group of military officers ruling a country after seizing power.

clue.text: You said girlfriend came round every year

indicators.note: said tells us to take the word by its sound rather than its spelling
to come round something is to surround it, so the outer pieces enclose the other

blocks.note: split in two: girl is a common name, Ann, and a friend is an ally
the letter U is pronounced like you

explanation.surface: Someone tells you that your girlfriend came round once a year.
explanation.walkthrough: Girlfriend must be split into girl and friend, which together go round the letter that sounds like you.
explanation.definitionFit: Annually is the adverb for something happening once each year.

clue.text: Let down by trade transfers around Europe

indicators.note: transfers moves things to new places, so these letters are shifted into a new order
around says the shuffled letters go about the abbreviation for the continent

blocks.note: both words taken as written
E is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: A football club feels let down by transfers of its players around Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To be betrayed is to be let down by someone who was trusted, a close synonym.

clue.text: Criminal who is said to know his way around the courts?

definitions.text: who is said to know his way around the courts?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone running a dishonest money-making scheme

blocks.clueFragment: who is said to know his way around the courts?
blocks.note: second meaning, playfully: a player handy with a racket on squash or tennis courts

explanation.walkthrough: Courts suggests law courts, which suits a criminal, but here they are sports courts where a racket is wielded.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs illegal rackets such as extortion, and the word puns on a racket-sports player.

clue.text: Continue to stand

blocks.note: first meaning: to last or carry on
second meaning: to tolerate or bear

explanation.walkthrough: Continue to stand looks like one phrase about staying upright; it is two separate verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to last over time and to put up with something unpleasant.

clue.text: Compelled to produce artificially by department

blocks.note: gardeners force rhubarb, growing it artificially early under cover
D is a standard abbreviation for department

explanation.surface: A department has been made to produce something artificially.
explanation.walkthrough: To force plants is to make them grow out of season with heat or darkness; 'by' places the abbreviation next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Forced means obliged or made to do something against one's will.

clue.text: Invests in cloth?

blocks.note: surface reading: puts money into textiles
setter's reading: the cloth is the clergy, and to invest is to install formally in office

explanation.walkthrough: The cloth is a set phrase for the clergy, from their distinctive dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop who makes someone a priest confers holy orders on them in a formal ceremony.

clue.text: Condescended, having planned to remove son

indicators.note: to remove means one letter is taken out of the word for planned

blocks.note: designed means planned
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone stooped low, having planned to get rid of their son.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to stoop to do something one considers beneath oneself, which is condescension.

clue.text: Tin Pan's stray?

blocks.note: surface reading: some lost animal belonging to a kitchen utensil
setter's reading: complete Tin Pan with its usual third word, New York's songwriting district, and add a homeless feline

explanation.walkthrough: Tin Pan Alley was the New York street of popular-music publishers; a stray belonging to that place would be its feline wanderer.
explanation.definitionFit: An alley cat is a stray urban cat living on the streets.

clue.text: Disinclined to have rave organised for the Kent area

indicators.note: organised means put into order, so these letters are arranged afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Kent is a county in the south-east of England, SE for short

explanation.surface: Someone is reluctant to have a rave party set up in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is the county in England's south-east corner.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or unwilling, so having a strong reluctance.

clue.text: Publication to promote growth of branch?

blocks.note: first meaning: a printed handout
second meaning, playfully: read as two words, allow foliage to sprout

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words and it becomes an instruction to let the greenery on a branch develop.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a small printed sheet handed out; it is also a little leaf on a branch.

clue.text: Mean to declare on time

blocks.note: to aver is to state or assert
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone intends to make an announcement on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Mean looks like a verb, intend, but it is the statistical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean is the arithmetic average of a set of numbers, a statistical synonym.

clue.text: He's in a night club? Could be sticky

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a dive is a seedy bar or nightclub
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a man is at a nightclub, hinting things could get awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase: sticky things could be glue-like, which the answer as an adjective describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Adhesive describes something able to stick fast to a surface, as glue or tape does.

clue.text: One hopes to catch early invader on the river

blocks.note: the Angles were Germanic people who invaded Britain in the fifth century
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone is hoping to catch an early invader on the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler is a fisherman, someone with rod and line who hopes to land fish.

clue.text: Make a profit without first reaping the corn

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of the word that follows it
without in its old sense means outside, so the profit word goes round

blocks.note: to gain is to make a profit
the first letter of reaping

explanation.surface: Farmers profit from the corn harvest without having to reap it.
explanation.walkthrough: Without looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside of.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain is cereal crop such as wheat, which in Britain is called corn.

clue.text: Reveal someone will not have father in wedding service?

definitions.text: someone will not have father in wedding service?

blocks.note: first meaning: to betray one's secret or feelings unintentionally

blocks.clueFragment: someone will not have father in wedding service?
blocks.note: second meaning, playfully: what a bride does with no father there to hand her over

explanation.walkthrough: At a traditional wedding the father gives the bride away; without him she must do it herself.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to let slip one's true identity or intentions, and literally describes self-handover at a wedding.

clue.text: A long walk and I'd rest, shattered

indicators.note: something shattered is broken into pieces, which can be put back in another order

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: After a long walk someone is exhausted and wants to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Shattered here looks like British slang for exhausted, which suits the walker; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step, and by extension a long walking pace.

clue.text: Posture can be altered in the outset

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters of the small container word are rearranged
in places one jumbled group inside the other

blocks.note: read as set out: the word set laid out in a new order
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's posture can be changed right from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: Outset reads as 'the start', but it splits into an anagram signal and a word to be jumbled; the loose wording makes this the trickiest parse.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is the way a person stands, their bodily posture or attitude.
